amendments.rule: An article governing a **substantival** demonstrative is its own `unrepresented` unit, and the demonstrative takes the whole English expression, including any generic noun the ASV supplies for it. `ὁ τοιοῦτος` → *such a one* gives *such a one* to the demonstrative headed on *such* and nothing to the article, as `τοὺς τοιούτους` → *such* and `τὰς τοιαύτας` → *such* do, and as `τοῖς τοιούτοις` → *unto such* does, the case preposition staying with the demonstrative under rule 21's determinerless clause because no determiner stands on the article to anchor it. This is rule 38's displacement holding where no head noun is expressed: what empties the article there is that another source word already occupies the English determiner slot, and a demonstrative does that whether or not it modifies a noun. Rule 38's closing clause speaks of `ταῦτα` standing with no article at all, and is not a licence to read the opposite where an article is present. What a demonstrative displaces is the **determiner slot** and nothing else, exactly as rule 20 has it, so an article whose determiner the demonstrative has taken is not thereby emptied of an English word of some other kind the ASV supplies for it. Where the ASV recasts the phrase as a finite relative clause and writes the article a separate **antecedent pronoun**, the article takes that pronoun and the demonstrative keeps the relativizer, any supplied copula and its own word: `τοὺς τοιούτους` → *them that are such* gives *them* to the article and *that are such* to the demonstrative, headed on *such*, exactly as rule 92 gives an antecedent pronoun to an article whose noun keeps the relativizer and rule 32 splits the same way before a participle. An antecedent pronoun is not a determiner, and a demonstrative cannot displace what is not one. The test is the ASV's and never the Greek's, the two constructions being identical in the source: where the ASV writes no such pronoun the article realizes nothing and the whole expression is the demonstrative's, which is why 1 Corinthians 16 leaves the article empty at 16:16 and aligns it at 16:18 while writing one analysis and not two. Do not manufacture an antecedent pronoun by reading one off a supplied generic noun — *such a one* is rule 17's completion of the demonstrative and not a pronoun the article may claim — and do not split *that are such* or *such a one* across the two tokens. Rule 22 is the contrast, and the test is whether a demonstrative is present: where the article's complement is an adjective or a participle nothing else can carry the determiner, so a supplied nominal is the article's own — `τὸ τρίτον` → *the third part* gives *the part* to the article and *third* to the adjective, and `οἱ ἡμέτεροι` → *our people* gives *people* to the article and *our* to the possessive adjective. Rule 17 then decides the head inside the demonstrative's unit exactly as it does for `ταῦτα` → *these things*: the generic noun expands the demonstrative, and the demonstrative stays the target head.
amendments.why: 1CO.16 writes the identical `article + substantival τοιοῦτος` twice with different ASV renderings — *unto such* at 16:16 and *them that are such* at 16:18 — and rule 49 as written covers only the first. Its unqualified 'takes the whole English expression' would force the second either to stretch *them* onto the demonstrative or to strand it, and the 16:18 pass had to reason around the rule and flagged the tension in its own review note. The qualification is not new law: rule 20's own text already says displacement empties the determiner slot and nothing else, and names a separate antecedent pronoun under rule 92 as something a displaced article still takes; rule 49 is expressly derived from rule 38's displacement, which is rule 20's, so it inherits that limit. Rule 92's corpus support is GAL.1.17 `τοὺς … ἀποστόλους` → *them that were*, JUD.1.12 `οἱ … σπιλάδες` → *they who are* and EPH.6.9's *he*, and rule 105 aligns a substantival `τοὺς` → *them that* at REV.13.6. Nothing in the amendment contradicts rule 49's own cited units — *such a one*, *such*, *such* — since in none of them does the ASV write a separate antecedent pronoun; the added sentence forbidding a pronoun read off a supplied generic noun keeps `ὁ τοιοῦτος` → *such a one* exactly where it stood. Returned as an amendment rather than a new rule so that the over-broad sentence is corrected where a verse pass will read it.

conventions: A supplied English pro-verb *do*, written where the ASV expands a bare Greek pronoun or crasis into a finite clause, rides with that pronoun and is neither `added` nor folded onto the lexical verb it echoes. `ὡς κἀγώ` → *as I also do* keeps *also do* with the crasis at 16:10, and `πάντα ὑμῶν` → *all that ye do* keeps *that ye do* with the genitive at 16:14, each headed on the pronominal word. 16:10 is rule 56's elliptical comparative, ἐργάζεται being already spent on *worketh*; 16:14 is the same judgment where no comparative stands, the genitive being the only token the supplied clause can belong to. Marking *do* `added` under rule 103 remains defensible in both.

προπέμπω is rendered by the whole idiom *set … forward on his journey* / *set … forward on my journey*, and the supplied possessive belongs inside the verb's own unit: no other source token licenses it, and the head is the verb word *set*, not *journey*. 16:6 and 16:11 read it alike, the preverb's *forward* staying inside the unit under rule 106 and the discontinuity permitted by rule 15.

The article before a substantival τοιοῦτος is decided by whether the ASV writes it a separate antecedent pronoun, not by the Greek, which is identical in both instances. 16:16 `τοῖς τοιούτοις` → *unto such* writes none, so the article is `unrepresented` under rule 49 and the case preposition stays with the demonstrative under rule 21's determinerless clause. 16:18 `τοὺς τοιούτους` → *them that are such* writes *them*, so the article takes it under rules 20 and 92 and the demonstrative keeps *that are such*, headed on *such*. Reading 16:18 by rule 49 alone — article empty, the whole expression on the demonstrative — remains defensible; rule 49 has been amended to record which way this chapter took it.

report: Checked all 38 candidate lemma groups and read the dump end to end for the added-unit blind spot. The chapter carries no `added` units at all (307 aligned, 14 unrepresented), so that blind spot is empty here, and no supplied word is folded in one verse and added in another.

Closest thing to a split is the article before a substantival τοιοῦτος: 16:16 `τοῖς τοιούτοις` → *unto such* leaves it unrepresented under rule 49, while 16:18 `τοὺς τοιούτους` → *them that are such* aligns it to *them* under rules 20 and 92. The Greek is identical, but the ASV writes a separate antecedent pronoun in one and not the other, and rule 20's antecedent clause decides both the same way. That is rule 24's habit and not two analyses, so no patch. I amended rule 49 instead: as written it reads absolutely, and a later pass reading it alone would empty 16:18's article and then have nowhere to put *them*.

Other candidates resolve as licensed by the ASV rather than by nothing. ἵνα → *that* four times and *to* twice is rule 40 realizing it by whatever word introduces the English clause, which rule 24 names. The T→PREP article pair splits on rule 31's own two arms: 16:1's `τῆς … εἰς` follows its noun with no supplied relative clause, 16:19's `τῇ κατ᾽ οἶκον` precedes its noun with one. The T→S pair at 16:17 and 16:18 turns on the same antecedent-pronoun test as 16:16/16:18. The negator with τις splits at 16:11 (*no* / *man*) and 16:22 (*not* / *any man*) because the negation sits in the determiner in one and on the verb in the other. κύριος at 16:10, 16:19 and 16:23 is rule 21 where an article stands and rule 51's anarthrous clause where none does.

All three BSB disagreements are documented convention differences and none is a genuine error. 16:2 ἐάν is rule 72's generalizing particle with no *-soever*, and that rule says in terms the report is not a correction. 16:4 τοῦ is rule 61's nominalizing article of an articular infinitive, the supplied *for* going to κἀμέ as the word it marks. 16:21 τῇ is displaced by the possessive adjective ἐμῇ under rule 54. No accepted edge was touched.

Heads are internally consistent: every support-verb frame heads on the word carrying the lexeme under rule 91 (*order*, *opportunity*, *subjection*, *store*, *men*), both προπέμπω idioms head on *set*, and both compound διέρχομαι units keep the preverb's *through* inside the verb under rule 106.

Three conventions recorded — the supplied pro-verb *do*, the προπέμπω idiom, and the τοιοῦτος article reconciliation. One amendment to rule 49; no new rules, the pro-verb and προπέμπω judgments each resting on two units of one chapter.
